# Overview {.unnumbered}

**ChromSimPipe** is a physics-based polymer simulation framework for testing
mechanistic hypotheses about 3D chromatin organisation. Given CTCF binding
data (CUT&Tag or ChIP-seq peaks) and Hi-C maps as input, it simulates
cohesin loop extrusion under different parameter conditions and compares the
resulting contact maps to your experimental Hi-C.

::: {.callout-note}
**Included example.** The default configuration ships with a use case from
the STRS project (Flores et al. 2026): HEK293T cells under hyperosmotic
stress (sorbitol treatment), comparing control vs. sorbitol CTCF CUT&Tag
peaks against matched Hi-C maps. Swap in your own data and the pipeline
runs the same way.
:::

## How the pieces fit together

```
  ChromSimSamplesheet.txt                      config/ChromSimConfig.yaml
  (one row per sample: metadata,               (loci, conditions, polysim,
   CTCF_Peaks, Hi-C)                            genome, motif, envs, outputDir)
          │                                               │
          └───────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                  ▼
                        configs/parameters.py
                                  │
                                  ▼
     convertHic ── getMotif ── preparePolysim      (shared by all loci)
                                  │
     orientCTCF ── validateCTCF ── ctcfOccupancy*        (per locus)
                                  │
     simulateShard (locus × condition × replicate × shard, GPU, polysim)
                                  │
                mergeShards (locus × condition × replicate)
                                  │
         analyzeCondition (locus × condition: contact map, P(s), APA,
               insulation, comparison with Hi-C)
                                  │
                                  ▼
                 output/loci/{locus}/analysis/{condition}/
```

## Example conditions

`config/ChromSimConfig.yaml` ships three example conditions comparing two
experimental states, `condition1` and `condition2`:

| # | Condition | Cohesin params | CTCF sites | Question |
|---|-----------|---------------|------------|----------|
| 1 | `cond1_baseline` | Gabriele 2022 | Condition 1 | Can we reproduce condition 1 Hi-C? |
| 2 | `cond2_ctcf-only` | Gabriele 2022 | Condition 2 | Do condition 2 CTCF sites alone explain condition 2 Hi-C? |
| 3 | `cond2_weak-ctcf` | Gabriele 2022 (0.5× capture) | Condition 2 | Weaker stalling at retained sites? |

## Example loci (STRS use case, hg38, HEK293T)

| Key | Chrom | Window | Genes |
|-----|-------|--------|-------|
| `chr1_fig1` | chr1 | 64.2 – 66.2 Mb | JAK1 / AK4 / LEPR |
| `chr4_fig1` | chr4 | 1.7 – 3.7 Mb | RNF4 / ADD1 / HTT |
| `chr6_fig1` | chr6 | 124.1 – 126.1 Mb | NKAIN2 / RNF217 |
| `chr16_sox8` | chr16 | 0.4 – 2.3 Mb | SOX8 |

## Cohesin model

The simulation models cohesin loop extrusion with the Hansen lab's polysim
package: cohesin rings load onto chromatin and extrude DNA into growing
loops, stalling when they meet CTCF sites from the correct direction, while a
3D polymer folds under those loops on a GPU. The defaults are the polysim
bootcamp tutorial values (after Gabriele et al. 2022 and Goel et al. 2025).

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| `lifetime` | 75,000 LEF timesteps | With `vlef` 0.0025, ~190 kb extruded per leg |
| `separation` | 240 monomers | ~8 cohesin rings per 2 Mb locus |
| `ctcf_capture` | 0.5 | 50% stalling probability per CTCF encounter |
| `polysim: life_boost_stalled` | 4 | Cohesin stalled at CTCF on both legs lives 4× longer |

Each condition can also switch on more of the model: no cohesin, CTCF
strength from peak signal, other factors such as YY1 or LDB1 as sticky
sites, chromatin compaction, and targeted cohesin loading or pausing. See
[Perturbation recipes](recipes.qmd) for examples and
[Configuration](configuration.qmd#every-condition-option) for every option.

## The tiling trick

Each locus is simulated as copies placed end to end on one ~70,000-monomer
chain (28 copies for the 2 Mb chr1 locus). This gives many times more contact
statistics per GPU run at no extra physics cost. Contact maps are folded back
to one locus-sized map for comparison. See Yang et al. 2023 *Nat Commun*.

## References

- Flores et al. 2026, STRS paper. GEO: GSE310051 (Hi-C), GSE310047 (CUT&Tag).
- Fudenberg et al., *Cell Reports* **15**:2038–2049 (2016). Canonical loop-extrusion model.
- Banigan et al., *eLife* **9**:e53558 (2020). LEF dynamics and CTCF barriers.
- Gabriele et al., *Science* **376**:496–501 (2022). Live-cell cohesin imaging (parameter source).
- Goel et al., *Nat Struct Mol Biol* (2025). Simulation code that polysim is based on.
- Hansen lab polysim bootcamp, <https://github.com/ahansenlab/polysim_bootcamp>. The simulation model ChromSimPipe runs.
- Yang et al., *Nat Commun* **14**:1913 (2023). Tiling trick for convergence.
